title: Present WTO appellate arrangements: China–US versus China–EU
scope_note: Bounded primary-source check; eight preserved original publications with exact selected reading scopes. No full DS611 merits or practical implementation audit; no general Chinese 2025 no-void undertaking verified or used. Current institutional webpages are retrieval-date snapshots.

sources.title: Appellate Body Members
sources.read_scope: Introductory institutional description and current-members statement; not a study of former-member biographies.
sources.exact_locators: Opening description and section Members of the Appellate Body and their respective terms of office.
sources.evidentiary_use: No current members and current inability to review appeals.
sources.limits: Undated current page captured on retrieval date; last-member expiry must not be confused with earlier loss of the three-member appellate quorum.

sources.title: Understanding on Rules and Procedures Governing the Settlement of Disputes
sources.read_scope: Complete Article 16 including footnote 7; Article 17.1–17.3; complete Article 25. Other provisions encountered during navigation are not credited as full reading.
sources.evidentiary_use: An appeal prevents consideration of panel adoption until completion; arbitration requires mutual agreement; parties abide by awards; Articles 21 and 22 apply with necessary adaptations.
sources.limits: Not a complete DSU reading or review of jurisprudence. Article 25 provides an available consensual route, not unilateral access against any member.

sources.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution Procedures
sources.read_scope: Complete substantive webpage, including Article 5, Article 25, MPIA participant list and listed awards, and mutually agreed solutions; dynamic underlying case lists not separately audited.
sources.exact_locators: Sections Article 25 arbitration and Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA).
sources.evidentiary_use: Current list includes China and the EU; United States absent. Arbitration can complement or replace other procedures by agreement.
sources.limits: Snapshot of listed participants, not an exhaustive review of each notification. No precise current membership count is used. No inference that a nonparticipant cannot separately consent to arbitration.

sources.title: DS611: China — Enforcement of intellectual property rights
sources.source_type: Official case summary and procedural chronology
sources.read_scope: Complete substantive case summary and chronology, including its summaries of panel and arbitral findings and disclaimer. No full underlying merits report is claimed read.
sources.exact_locators: Panel and Appellate Body proceedings; Arbitration under Article 25 of the DSU; Reasonable period of time.
sources.evidentiary_use: Records bilateral consent, each appeal and the issued award.
sources.limits: Informational summary, not authoritative interpretation. Its implementation chronology ends in August 2025 and does not establish the absence of later action; APP-07 and APP-08 supply subsequent statements.

sources.title: China — Enforcement of Intellectual Property Rights: Arbitration under Article 25 of the DSU, Award of the Arbitrators, Addendum (WT/DS611/ARB25/Add.1)
sources.author_or_institution: World Trade Organization; agreed procedure of China and European Union
sources.source_type: Original bilateral procedural agreement reproduced in official award addendum
sources.read_scope: Cover and contents; complete Annex A-1, paragraphs 1–19 and all footnotes, printed/PDF pages 4–6. Remaining addendum not fully read.
sources.exact_locators: Annex A-1 / WT/DS611/7, pp. 4–6; especially paragraphs 1–2, 6, 15 and 17.
sources.evidentiary_use: Case-specific conditional Article 25 appeal; fallback against ordinary appeal; agreement to abide by final award; notification without DSB adoption; implementation provisions.
sources.limits: The agreement does not establish Chinese consent to arbitration with every member, a universal no-void commitment, endorsement of subsequent arbitral reasoning or domestic performance.

sources.title: DS543: United States — Tariff Measures on Certain Goods from China
sources.source_type: Official case summary and procedural chronology
sources.read_scope: Complete substantive summary and chronology, including panel findings and final displayed appeal entry; no full panel report or appeal notice claimed read.
sources.exact_locators: Panel and Appellate Body proceedings, final paragraph dated 26 October 2020.
sources.evidentiary_use: Concrete US appeal in a dispute brought by China.
sources.limits: Summary is not authoritative legal interpretation or a prediction of future US decisions. No inference of absence of later negotiation solely from the final dated entry.

sources.title: Following WTO ruling favourable to EU, China announces withdrawal of its anti-suit injunction policy
sources.author_or_institution: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
sources.read_scope: Complete substantive news release and publication metadata, including distinction from a separate standard-essential-patent dispute.
sources.exact_locators: Paragraphs beginning Following the issuance of the award and Given the unwritten nature.
sources.evidentiary_use: Commission acknowledges reported withdrawal and accessibility of Chinese notice while continuing to monitor compliance.
sources.limits: An interested party’s assessment. Underlying court notice and practical effect not separately audited; continued monitoring is not itself a finding of noncompliance.

sources.title: Minutes of meeting held on 26 September 2025 (WT/DSB/M/505), item 2: China — Enforcement of Intellectual Property Rights (DS611)
sources.author_or_institution: WTO Dispute Settlement Body; attributed statements of China, EU and other members
sources.source_type: Official minutes of primary party statements
sources.read_scope: Cover metadata and complete item 2, paragraphs 2.1–2.10, printed/PDF pages 6–9, including footnote 3. Other agenda items not counted as a complete reading.
sources.exact_locators: China: paragraphs 2.2–2.4, pp. 6–8; EU: paragraph 2.5, pp. 8–9.
sources.evidentiary_use: Chinese objection to reasoning alongside implementation claim; EU’s contemporaneous refusal to accept full implementation on available information.
sources.limits: Attributed meeting minutes are not a verbatim transcript or compliance judgment. Do not generalize China’s case-specific reported conduct into a universal undertaking. Full substantive award, court notice and later court conduct not independently audited.
